decisions.tier_rule: Tier 2 by the path-glob table: behaviour changes are confined to src/tour/quality_rubric.py (the src/tour/ row). tests/ is Tier 1; specs/*.md is Tier 0. No Makefile, no .claude/, no deploy, no DB/data write, no frontend. Tier 2 => skeptic panel P=2, acceptance runs.
decisions.the_complaint: A real Opus 60-min Paris tour generated in the workbench on 2026-07-26 is genuinely good (6 dense stops, 2827 words, 18.8 min of speech) and the rubric branded it '✗ FAILS the standard' with a C3-thin BLOCKER, which blocks SERVING. The owner's position is that the rubric is wrong, not the tour. The evidence below agrees.
decisions.root_cause: C3-thin's floor is duration_min * ERR_SHORT(0.83) * AUDIO_FRACTION(0.60) * AUDIO_FLOOR_FRAC(0.8) = 0.398 * duration. routing.py:44-45 declares WALK_FRACTION=0.40 + AUDIO_FRACTION=0.60 = 1.00 — a DISJOINT walk-XOR-listen time model, i.e. it assumes the tourist stands still for 60% of the hour. That model was superseded by the owner's own ruling (commit 4cbb94c) that leg audio OVERLAPS walking and costs ZERO elapsed time. C7 and C7b were updated for the ruling (they measure 'walk + STATIONARY listening'); C3 never was. C3 is a fossil of a walk-in-silence world.
decisions.measured_verdict_on_the_projects_own_cer: DECISIVE, and it needs no paid run. data/certification/tour-batch-v1/ is a git-tracked, real-Opus (model claude-opus-4-8, provenance provider_response, self-verifying artifact/response/customer_text sha256) batch of 8 authored tours across 2 cities and 2 durations. Scored with the REAL score_tour today: 7 of 8 FAIL C3-thin. Ratios (audio/duration): nyc-central-park-90 0.249, nyc-grand-central-60 0.287, nyc-lower-manhattan-90 0.228, nyc-village-loop-60 0.311, paris-ile-90 0.343, paris-marais-60 0.277, paris-pont-neuf-60 0.427 (the only PASS), paris-west-axis-90 0.056 (genuinely starved: 2 stops, 5.0 min of audio, 85 min of walking). The healthy population is 0.227-0.427; the current floor demands 0.398. The rubric fails the project's own certification batch.
decisions.the_check_is_inverted: Across the 191 real Script dumps in data/paris/tours/ (untracked, recomputed with today's meter) 183/191 fail C3; 0/36 at 90 min and 0/4 at 120 min ever pass; the richest tour ever produced (11 stops, 5796 words, 38.6 min) reaches 54% of its floor. Meanwhile TWO of the 8 tours that DO pass are ONE-STOP tours (20.2 min of audio at a single stop). C3 as written passes a 1-stop tour and blocks an 11-stop one — inverted relative to its stated purpose.
decisions.second_contradiction_structural: C3's floor is LINEAR in duration while word capacity is BOUNDED at max_stops * per-stop cap (8 * 750 = 6000 words = 40 min). TourInput.duration_min allows le=600 (contract.py:49). So the 0.398 floor is structurally unsatisfiable above ~100 min for ANY choice of fraction — no re-pick of the constant fixes it, which is why the repair needs a cap term, not just a smaller number.
decisions.third_contradiction_doc: specs/2026-07-19-tour-quality-standard/01-standard.md:325 cites MAX_WORDS_PER_STATION=250 (~2 min, sourced to Nubart). 8 stops * 250 = 2000 words = 13.3 min, BELOW the 23.9-min floor: C3 is unsatisfiable while obeying the standard's own cited station cap. The measured accepted tours run median 644 words/stop (2.6x that cap), so the cap is descriptive of museums, not walking tours.
decisions.the_owner_already_pre_authorised_this: 01-standard.md:315-320 says verbatim: 'AUDIO_FRACTION = 0.60 is cited below against a Nubart figure that actually says 0.50, and the 0.8 C3 floor is derived from it. Both were set in a walk-in-silence world. Now that leg audio is free, the floor should be re-derived — a stop-audio floor and a leg-fill target are arguably two different numbers. Do not treat 0.60/0.80 as settled.' This slice closes that open item.
decisions.c8_also_blocks_real_tours: GORGE_MAX_WORDS_PER_STOP=750 (quality_rubric.py:63) fires on 3 of 8 certified tours. Measured widest-stop population: 661/662/664/673/679/757/761/808. Recalibrating to 850 clears the real ceiling (808) while still catching the defect the cap exists for (the Notre-Dame 1022-1038-word stop, at 1.22x). Without this, fixing C3 alone still leaves good tours blocked.
decisions.c3_has_zero_tests: grep -rn 'C3-thin' tests/ returns only a comment (test_tour_quality_rubric.py:131) and a compose_fixable parametrize entry (:1069). Deleting the entire C3 block leaves the suite GREEN — violating that file's own docstring contract that 'Every test here is a DISCRIMINATOR'. This slice adds the first real C3 tests.
decisions.severity_decision_c3_stays_blocker: REJECTED: demoting C3 to WARN (the C12 precedent at quality_rubric.py:99). The C12 demotion trigger was 'a BLOCKER here refuses to serve the gold-standard tour'. After recalibration that trigger is absent — zero real tours are refused — while the requirement to catch a starved tour (the documented 2-stop/9.4-min run, and paris-west-axis-90) demands a BLOCKER. Calibrating is strictly better than demoting: demotion would leave NO thinness blocker at all and would bless a 1-stop 4.6-min tour sold as 60 minutes.
decisions.refuted_alternative: REFUTED BY DATA, do not adopt: 'mirror C7 — measure STATIONARY audio against STATIONARY capacity (err_short_total - walk)'. Measured stationary fill: healthy tours 0.65-0.96 of capacity; the starved paris-west-axis-90 is 1.06, because routing left it almost no stop time. That reformulation BLESSES the starved tour. The overlap ruling's real consequence is narrower — it removes the justification for deriving a floor from a walk/audio partition, not the need for an aggregate floor.
decisions.c3b_leg_silence_deferred: The PO recommended also adding C3b-leg-silence (WARN) so the tour's one true defect stays visible: measured leg fill is 0.001-0.040 across all 8 certified tours, i.e. every tour ever produced walks in >=96% silence. DEFERRED from this slice on the manager's call, and this is an escalation for the human. At any useful threshold it fires on 8/8 tours including the accepted one, which is exactly the zero-signal failure C9-long-sentences and C10-no-look-cue already exhibit (both also fire on 8/8). Adding a third always-red warning makes the panel less trustworthy, not more. The leg-silence check should ship in the SAME slice as the leg-fill fix (overflow_by_poi already holds enough on-lens material to fill 20-46% of the dead air at ~83s/leg), where it can be a meaningful gate rather than wallpaper.
decisions.no_paid_run_needed: The accepted anchor already exists in tracked data. nyc-village-loop-60 (5 stops / 2803 words / 18.7 min / 60-min request / ratio 0.311) is a structural twin of the owner's 2026-07-26 tour (6 stops / 2827 words / 18.8 min / ratio 0.313), and paris-marais-loop-60 (0.277) plus nyc-village-loop-60 (0.311) bracket it from both sides. The negative pole (paris-west-axis-90, 0.056) is in the same tracked corpus. Zero provider spend for the whole ledger.
decisions.fixture_mechanism_is_not_new: Proven-not-new: data/certification/tour-batch-v1/ is already git-tracked (62 files) and .gitignore:302-303 states verbatim that the paid evaluator receipts are ignored but 'Keep the authored tour batch (tour-batch-v1) visible for regression tests' — the intent is already declared. The Sentence reconstruction already exists at scripts/tour_batch_review.py:401-405 (Sentence.model_validate(json.loads(receipt['raw_response']))) and is already exercised by tests/test_tour_batch_review_runner.py. The min(linear_floor, share_of_gorge_cap) construction already exists verbatim for C1 at quality_rubric.py:467-470, with STARVE_FLOOR_MAX_SHARE_OF_CAP's own docstring (:107-110) saying 'so C1 and C8 can never demand contradictory things' — S3 applies that ratified pattern to C3. MAX_COMPOSED_STOPS names a number already asserted at premium_tour.py:232 and routing.py:78. Rejected alternatives: fixtures/tour_golden/*.json holds no sentences and no audio (selection/routing only, and needs live Neo4j); tools/compose_snapshot.py would cost ~$1 and its capture dir does not exist; data/*/tours/ is gitignored as 'machine-local reproduction output, never committed'.
decisions.out_of_scope: Do NOT touch src/tour/routing.py — WALK_FRACTION/AUDIO_FRACTION/ERR_SHORT still legitimately drive the selection fill pass (selection.py:2447), the move ceiling (:2511) and density.py:400 as PLANNING heuristics, and tests/test_tour_routing.py::test_pace_constants_lock pins their sum. The fix is to stop the RUBRIC deriving a serving verdict from them. Also out: fixing the silent walks (separate slice); enabling a paid compose repair loop on thinness; C1/C2/C4/C5/C6/C7b/C9/C10/C11/C12 recalibration (C9 and C10 fire on 8/8 real tours and are separately miscalibrated — flagged, not fixed); a stop-count floor (real gap, nothing blocks a verbose 1-stop tour, deferred); any frontend change (the panel at review.html:3350-3385 is already generic over blockers/warnings); any paid regeneration, tour re-scoring backfill, cloud or prod write.
decisions.close_gate_out_of_engine_scope: AC-11 (make lint zero errors + make test green, 0 failures, 0 skips) is the run's CLOSE GATE, which the engine performs once as `make audit` rather than as a step. It is deliberately not carried by any step's criterion_ids.

acceptance_criteria.text: Given each of the 7 healthy tours in the tracked data/certification/tour-batch-v1/ corpus, when score_tour runs, then no finding with check == 'C3-thin' is returned.
Given paris-west-axis-90 (2 stops, 5.0 min of audio for a 90-min request, ratio 0.056), when score_tour runs, then exactly one finding with check == 'C3-thin' is returned at Severity.BLOCKER.
Given a Script reproducing the documented starved run (2 stops, 60-min request, total_audio_seconds 564 = 9.4 min, ratio 0.157), then a C3-thin finding is returned at Severity.BLOCKER.

For every offered duration 1..600 (TourInput allows le=600), the C3 floor in words is <= MAX_COMPOSED_STOPS * GORGE_MAX_WORDS_PER_STOP — C3 can never demand more words than C8 forbids. This is what makes the floor satisfiable at 90/120/240/600 min.
src.tour.quality_rubric no longer imports or references AUDIO_FRACTION or ERR_SHORT from src.tour.routing — the rubric derives no serving verdict from a planning constant of the engine it judges.

Given the widest stop measured in the certified corpus (808 words), no C8-gorged finding is returned; given a 1038-word stop (the real Notre-Dame defect the cap exists to catch), C8-gorged IS still returned.

All 8 certified cases reconstruct from git-tracked data into scoreable (Script, Route) pairs, and their computed audio minutes are exactly 22.4 / 17.2 / 20.5 / 18.7 / 30.9 / 16.6 / 25.6 / 5.0 — pinning the EVIDENCE independently of any threshold.

Given a Route stamped at the certification planning budget (nominal fraction 1.00, i.e. 3600 s for a 60-min request), the C7 message states the ceiling the route was actually planned to (100%), not the hardcoded '83% of the requested duration' it interpolates from ERR_SHORT today.

Every calibration anchor path resolves under a git-tracked location; no anchor resolves under data/*/tours/, which .gitignore:301 marks 'machine-local reproduction output, never committed' and which would therefore pass here and fail on a fresh clone.

For all 8 certified cases, the set of finding ids before and after this slice differs ONLY in ids starting 'C3' or 'C8'. Any change to a C1/C2/C4/C5/C6/C7/C7b/C9/C10/C11/C12 finding on any anchor fails this criterion.

steps.name: Reconstruct the tracked certification corpus as a $0 rubric fixture
Recalibrate the C8 gorge cap against the widest real stop
Re-base the C3 floor on measured delivered audio, not the disjoint model
Cap the C3 floor so it can never outrun C8 at any offered duration
